title: Finite normal extensions agree if their dense open restrictions agree
statement: Let L be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and n:N→L and p:E→L finite morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose every local ring of N and E is a normal domain (domain and integrally closed) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let U be open in L with dense inverse images in both N and E. For any isomorphism e:N|U ≅ E|U over U, there exists an isomorphism e′:N ≅ E over L.

proof.text: The finite morphisms imply the source schemes are locally Noetherian. Their domain stalks imply they are reduced. Apply isIso_fromNormalization_denseOpen to the dense opens V=n^{-1}U and W=p^{-1}U to identify the relative normalizations of their inclusions with N and E.

Use the given isomorphism e over U to form a map V to E over L, then the pair of this map with V→N gives a map V→E×_L N. The second projection is finite, hence integral. Mathlib normalizationDesc extends the pair through the relative normalization of V→N; compose with the inverse of its canonical isomorphism to N and with the first projection to obtain f:N→E, with f;p=n and V.ι;f=e.hom;W.ι. Apply the same construction to e.inv to obtain g:E→N. This uses the canonical normalization and its inverse, not arbitrary data chosen from an existence hole.

The composites f;g and g;f restrict to identities on V and W, by the two extension equations and the inverse identities for e. The source schemes are reduced, their dense open inclusions are dominant, and n and p are separated because they are finite. Mathlib ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated therefore identifies these composites with the global identities. Package f and g as an isomorphism over L.

theorem finite_normal_iso_of_dense_open
    {L N E : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian L]
    (n : N ⟶ L) (p : E ⟶ L) [IsFinite n] [IsFinite p]
    (hnormal : ∀ z : N, IsDomain (N.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (N.presheaf.stalk z))
    (henormal : ∀ z : E, IsDomain (E.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (E.presheaf.stalk z))
    (U : L.Opens)
    (hn : Dense (↑(n ⁻¹ᵁ U) : Set N))
    (hp : Dense (↑(p ⁻¹ᵁ U) : Set E))
    (e : (n ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ≅ (p ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)
    (he : e.hom ≫ (p ∣_ U) = n ∣_ U) :
    ∃ e' : N ≅ E, e'.hom ≫ p = n
